extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO officials (U.S. patent practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory requirements and procedures governing issuance of U.S. patents, patent contents, patent term, patent term adjustments, provisional rights, and patent-term extensions (35 U.S.C. §§151–156 and related provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of allowance and issue fee payment
rubrics_metrics.description: If it appears that an applicant is entitled to a patent under the law, a written notice of allowance of the application shall be given or mailed to the applicant. The notice shall specify a sum, constituting the issue fee and any required publication fee, which shall be paid within 3 months thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon payment of this sum the patent may issue, but if payment is not timely made, the application shall be regarded as abandoned. (35 U.S.C. 151(a)-(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of patent to assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents may be granted to the assignee of the inventor of record in the Patent and Trademark Office, upon the application made and the specification sworn to by the inventor, except as otherwise provided in this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment to an assignee is permissible where the inventor has executed the application and sworn to the specification; other statutory exceptions may apply. (35 U.S.C. 152)

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and drawing as part of patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the specification and drawing shall be annexed to the patent and be a part of such patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification and drawings appended to the patent become part of the patent document and define its particulars. (Referenced in 35 U.S.C. 152/related provisions)

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents shall be issued in the name of the United States of America, under the seal of the Patent and Trademark Office, and shall be signed by the Director or have his signature placed thereon and shall be recorded in the Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal requirements for execution and recording of granted patents. (35 U.S.C. 153)

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent contents — title and grant language
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent shall contain a short title of the invention and a grant to the patentee, his heirs or assigns, of the right to exclude others from making, using, offering for sale, or selling the invention throughout the United States or importing the invention into the United States, and, if the invention is a process, of the right to exclude others from using, offering for sale or selling throughout the United States, or importing into the United States, products made by that process, referring to the specification for the particulars thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory description of required grant language and linkage to the specification. (35 U.S.C. 154(a)(1))

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term — basic rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the payment of fees under this title, the grant shall be for a term beginning on the date on which the patent issues and ending 20 years from the date on which the application for the patent was filed in the United States or, if the application contains a specific reference to an earlier filed application under sections 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c), from the date on which the earliest such application was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 20-year patent term measured from U.S. filing date (with specific rules for continuations/priority under certain sections). (35 U.S.C. 154(a)(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority exclusions in term calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority under section 119, 365(a), 365(b), 386(a), or 386(b) shall not be taken into account in determining the term of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain foreign or other priority claims do not alter the 20-year term calculation. (35 U.S.C. 154(a)(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term adjustment for USPTO delays — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If the issue of an original patent is delayed due to the failure of the Patent and Trademark Office to: (i) provide at least one of the notifications under section 132 or a notice of allowance under section 151 not later than 14 months after certain filing dates; (ii) respond to a reply under section 132 or to an appeal under section 134 within 4 months; (iii) act on an application within 4 months after certain Board or court decisions where allowable claims remain; or (iv) issue a patent within 4 months after payment of the issue fee and satisfaction of outstanding requirements, the term of the patent shall be extended 1 day for each day after the end of the specified period until the action is taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate guarantees address timely notifications, responses, actions after decisions, and issuing after fee payment; each day of PTO delay can result in a 1-day extension. (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(A)-(iv))

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term adjustment for long pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: If the issue of an original patent is delayed due to the failure of the USPTO to issue a patent within 3 years after the actual filing date (excluding time consumed by applicant-requested continued examination, certain proceedings, or applicant-requested processing delays), the term of the patent shall be extended 1 day for each day after the end of that 3-year period until the patent is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 3-year pendency guarantee subject to exclusions for applicant delays and certain proceedings. (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(B))

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term adjustment for interferences/secrecy/appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: If the issue of an original patent is delayed due to a proceeding under section 135(a), the imposition of an order under section 181 (secrecy order), or appellate review by the PTAB or a Federal court reversing an adverse determination of patentability, the term of the patent shall be extended 1 day for each day of the pendency of the proceeding, order, or review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments apply for delays resulting from specified special PTO or national security proceedings and appeals. (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(C))

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on patent term adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent that periods of delay attributable to grounds specified overlap, the period of any adjustment shall not exceed the actual number of days the issuance of the patent was delayed. No patent term may be adjusted beyond a date disclaimed. The period of adjustment shall be reduced by periods during which the applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoids double-counting overlapping delays; prevents adjustment beyond disclaimed term dates; reductions apply where applicant's lack of reasonable efforts contributed to delay. (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(4)(A)-(C) and related subsections)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for applicant failure to engage in reasonable efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment shall be reduced by a period equal to the period of time during which the applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution of the application. For adjustments under the 3-year pendency rule, an applicant shall be deemed to have failed to engage in reasonable efforts for the cumulative total of any periods of time in excess of 3 months that are taken to respond to a notice from the Office requesting any rejection, objection, argument, or other request, measuring such 3-month period from the date the notice was given or mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines how applicant delays in responding (especially repeatedly exceeding 3 months) reduce PTO-caused adjustment; Director will prescribe circumstances that constitute failure to engage. (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(4)(C)(i)-(ii) and related)

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's procedures and applicant reconsideration for term adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall make a determination of the period of any patent term adjustment and transmit notice no later than the date of issuance of the patent, and provide the applicant one opportunity to request reconsideration of any patent term adjustment determination. The Director shall prescribe regulations establishing procedures for application and determination of patent term adjustments. The Director shall reinstate up to three additional months of adjustment if the applicant, prior to issuance, shows that despite all due care the applicant was unable to respond within the 3‑month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative procedural protections: notice, one reconsideration opportunity, regulatory procedures, and limited reinstatement for excusable applicant delays. (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)-(3) and related)

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive civil action for adjustment reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant dissatisfied with the Director's decision on the applicant's request for reconsideration shall have exclusive remedy by a civil action against the Director filed in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia within 180 days after the Director's decision; chapter 7 of title 5 applies to such action. Any final judgment changing the period of adjustment shall be served on the Director and the Director shall alter the term accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies exclusive judicial remedy, venue, timing, and effect of final judgments on patent term. (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(3)(A))

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rights — right to reasonable royalty from publication to issue
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall include the right to obtain a reasonable royalty from any person who, during the period beginning on the date of publication of the application and ending on the date the patent is issued, (A)(i) makes, uses, offers for sale, or sells in the U.S. the invention as claimed in the published patent application or imports such an invention, or (ii) if the invention claimed in the published application is a process, uses/offers/sells/imports products made by that process; and (B) had actual notice of the published patent application (for foreign-language international publications, the person had a translation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional rights entitle the patentee to reasonable royalties for infringing acts during the pre‑grant publication window, but only with actual notice (and translation if necessary). (35 U.S.C. 154(d)(1))

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantially identical claims requirement for provisional rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to obtain a reasonable royalty shall not be available unless the invention as claimed in the patent is substantially identical to the invention as claimed in the published patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional rights require substantial identity between published claims and issued claims; protects against claim scope changes. (35 U.S.C. 154(d)(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limitation on actions to obtain provisional-right royalties
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to obtain a reasonable royalty under provisional rights shall be available only in an action brought not later than 6 years after the patent is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute of limitations-like cap on recovery for provisional-right damages. (35 U.S.C. 154(d)(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: International-application provisional-rights requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For an international application published in a language other than English, the right to obtain a reasonable royalty based on the publication commences on the date the PTO receives a translation of the publication into English; the Director may require the applicant to provide a copy of the international application and a translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures actual notice is meaningful for foreign-language publications; PTO can request copies/translations. (35 U.S.C. 154(d)(4))

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for patent-term extension (PTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a patent that claims a product, a method of using a product, or a method of manufacturing a product shall be extended if: (1) the term has not expired before an application for extension is submitted; (2) the term has never been extended under subsection (e)(1); (3) an application for extension is submitted by the owner of record or its agent and in accordance with subsection (d) requirements; (4) the product has been subject to a regulatory review period before its commercial marketing or use; and (5) except as provided, the permission for commercial marketing or use after such regulatory review period is the first permitted commercial marketing or use of the product under the law under which the regulatory review occurred (with specific exceptions for certain recombinant DNA and animal drug cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the basic statutory eligibility conditions for obtaining a regulatory-review-based patent-term extension. (35 U.S.C. 156(a)(1)-(5))

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of rights during patent-term extension
rubrics_metrics.description: During the period the term of the patent is extended, the rights derived from the patent shall be limited: (1) for patents claiming a product, to any use approved for the product before expiration and on or after the expiration of the regulatory review period upon which the extension was based; (2) for patents claiming a method of using a product, to any use claimed by the patent and approved for the product as described; (3) for patents claiming a method of manufacturing, limited to the method of manufacturing as used to make the approved product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension does not broaden claimed rights beyond approved uses and approved manufacturing methods; rights tied to regulatory approvals. (35 U.S.C. 156(b)(1)-(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction and limits on period of extension
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a patent eligible for extension shall be extended by the regulatory review period occurring after patent issuance, except that: (1) each regulatory review period shall be reduced by any period during which the applicant did not act with due diligence; (2) after reduction, the period of extension shall include only one-half of the time remaining in certain specified regulatory periods; and (3) if the remaining patent term after approval plus the regulatory review period exceeds 14 years, the extension shall be reduced so the total does not exceed fourteen years; and (4) no more than one patent may be extended for the same regulatory review period for any product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps extension lengths to prevent excessive extension and apportions reductions for applicant delay; ensures only one patent per regulatory review period gets extended. (35 U.S.C. 156(c) and related)

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents for patent-term extension
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain an extension, the owner of record or agent shall submit an application within the 60-day period beginning on the date the product received permission for commercial marketing/use (with certain drug-specific timing exceptions). The application shall contain: (A) the identity of the approved product and the Federal statute under which regulatory review occurred; (B) the identity of the patent and each claim of such patent which claims the approved product or a method of using or manufacturing the approved product; (C) information to enable the Director to determine eligibility and the period of extension and to enable the Director and the Secretary of HHS or Agriculture to determine the period; (D) a brief description of activities undertaken by the applicant during the regulatory review period with significant dates; and (E) such patent or other information as the Director may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the documentary and factual content the PTO expects in a PTE application, including coordination with HHS/USDA for period determination. (35 U.S.C. 156(d)(1)(A)-(E))

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency notification and regulatory-review determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days of submittal of the extension application, the Director shall notify the Secretary of Agriculture (for certain products) or the Secretary of Health and Human Services (for other regulated products) and submit a copy of the application. Not later than 30 days after receipt, the Secretary shall review the dates in the application, determine the applicable regulatory review period, notify the Director, and publish in the Federal Register a notice of such determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes interagency notice/coordination and public notice requirements for determining the regulatory-review period used to calculate the PTE. (35 U.S.C. 156(d)(2)(A))

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition process and due-diligence determination by Secretary
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition is submitted that the applicant did not act with due diligence during the applicable regulatory review period, the Secretary must determine if the applicant acted with due diligence within specified timeframes (not later than 90 days after receipt of the petition and not later than 180 days after publication of the Secretary's determination on which the petition is based). For FDA matters, the authority to make this determination may not be delegated below the Office of the Director of Food and Drugs; similar non-delegation applies for USDA. The Secretary shall notify the Director and publish the determination and factual/legal basis, and may hold an informal hearing on request within 60 days of publication, conducting it within specified timeframes; the Secretary shall affirm or revise the determination within 30 days after the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedural protections and timelines for third-party challenges alleging lack of due diligence and ensures senior-level review at HHS/USDA. (35 U.S.C. 156(d)(2)(B))

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of due diligence for PTE
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of paragraph (2)(B), the term 'due diligence' means that degree of attention, continuous directed effort, and timeliness as may reasonably be expected from, and are ordinarily exercised by, a person during a regulatory review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory standard for measuring applicant behavior during regulatory review; used to assess reductions in extensions. (35 U.S.C. 156(d)(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirements for PTE applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for the extension of the term of a patent is subject to the disclosure requirements prescribed by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may require additional disclosures in the PTE application; applicants must follow PTO disclosure rules. (35 U.S.C. 156(d)(4))

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim extensions when regulatory review may extend past patent expiry
rubrics_metrics.description: If the owner reasonably expects that the applicable regulatory review period may extend beyond the expiration of the patent term, the owner or its agent may submit an application for an interim extension during the period beginning 6 months and ending 15 days before the term is due to expire. The application shall contain: (i) identity of product and statute under review; (ii) identity of the patent and claims; (iii) information to enable Director to determine eligibility; (iv) a brief description of activities undertaken during the review to date and significant dates; and (v) such patent or other information as the Director may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows seeking temporary protection when approval timelines risk rendering the patent expired before final extension determination. (35 U.S.C. 156(d)(5)(A))

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates and limits for interim extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director determines that except for permission to market or use the product commercially the patent would be eligible for extension, the Director shall publish a notice and issue a certificate of interim extension for a period of not more than 1 year. The owner may apply for not more than 4 subsequent interim extensions (with specific exceptions) and each certificate shall be recorded in the official file and considered part of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim extensions are limited in duration and number; must be published and recorded; special limits exist for certain categories. (35 U.S.C. 156(d)(5)(B)-(D))

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination and further extension conditions for interim extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interim extension terminates at the end of the 60-day period beginning on the date the product receives permission for commercial marketing or use, except that if within that 60-day period the applicant notifies the Director of such permission and submits additional information not previously contained in the application, the patent shall be further extended in accordance with the section—for not to exceed 5 years from the original expiration date or, in certain cases, from the date the product receives approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the interplay between interim certificates and final extension decisions, including caps on total further extension and timing rules. (35 U.S.C. 156(d)(5)(E))

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of rights during interim extension
rubrics_metrics.description: The rights derived from any patent the term of which is extended under the interim-extension paragraph shall, during the period of interim extension, be limited: (i) for a patent claiming a product, to any use then under regulatory review; (ii) for a patent claiming a method of using a product, to any use claimed by the patent then under regulatory review; and (iii) for a patent claiming a method of manufacturing, to the method of manufacturing as used to make the product then under regulatory review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim extension rights are narrow and tied to the specific uses/manufacturing methods under active review. (35 U.S.C. 156(d)(5)(F))

rubrics_metrics.name: Director determination based on representations and interim extension if patent would expire
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination that a patent is eligible for extension may be made by the Director solely on the basis of the representations in the application. If the Director determines the patent is eligible and requirements complied with, the Director shall issue a certificate of extension under seal for the prescribed period and record it. If the patent would expire before a certificate of extension is issued or denied, the Director shall extend the patent for periods of up to one year if he determines the patent is eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may rely on applicant representations for issuing PTE certificates and may grant temporary one-year extensions to avoid gaps pending final determination. (35 U.S.C. 156(e)(1)-(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions used for PTE — product and drug product
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of section 156: (1) 'product' includes (A) a drug product, and (B) any medical device, food additive, or color additive subject to regulation under the FD&C Act; (2) 'drug product' means the active ingredient of a new drug, antibiotic drug, or human biological product (as those terms are used in the FD&C Act and the Public Health Service Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory definitions clarify which regulated articles are 'products' eligible for patent-term extension. (35 U.S.C. 156(f)(1)-(2))
